data.narrative:
Compound Eye is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jason Devitt and Haoyang Wang that has raised $20.6M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable (277810.KQ), including same-stage roboticists such as Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses total raised ($21M) as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $39M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—produces a median of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

The wide spread between methods ($39M to $1.8B) reflects a fundamental tension: stage-progression anchored to historical capital deployed suggests early-stage valuation, while peer comparables indicate material value creation or market premium in downstream robotics. The triangulated range spans $33M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $895M. Key uncertainties include whether Compound Eye's technology trajectory and market position justify peer-median valuations or whether the company remains closer to capital-deployed benchmarks. Investor conviction on product differentiation and go-to-market progress will materially narrow this range.
